name: Example: Computing the Normal Line to a Parametric Curve
problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14043931/assets/9dcc4c97bd296ef4627b02b6cfafcdb643f475cd8dacd36a820db760bd6fb045.png)

The following parametric equations define the curve shown above:

$$
x=2\cos{t} +\sin{2t},\quad y=\cos{t} - 2\sin{2t},\qquad 0\leq t<2\pi
$$

Calculate the equation of the normal to the curve at the point where $t=\dfrac{\pi}{4}$ (shown as a dashed line in the plot above).
worked_solution:
First, we find the coordinates of the point by substituting $t=\dfrac{\pi}{4}$ into the parametric equations:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =2\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})+\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\cdot \frac{\pi }{4}) \\  & =2\cdot \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}+\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}) \\  & =\sqrt{2}+1, \\  \\ y & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})-2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\cdot \frac{\pi }{4}) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}-2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}-2(1) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}-2.\end{aligned}
$$

So we're looking to find the equation of the normal at the point $\left(\sqrt{2}+1,\dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{2} -2\right).$ For this, we need to find $\dfrac{\textrm{d}y}{\textrm{d}x},$ which means we first need to find the derivatives of $x$ and $y,$ as follows:

$$
x'(t) = -2\sin t + 2\cos 2t, \qquad y'(t) = -\sin t - 4 \cos 2t .
$$

So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dy}{dx} & =\frac{{y}^{′}(t)}{{x}^{′}(t)} \\  & =\frac{-\operatorname{sin}⁡t-4\operatorname{cos}⁡2t}{-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t+2\operatorname{cos}⁡2t} \\  & =-\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡t+4\operatorname{cos}⁡2t}{2(\operatorname{cos}⁡2t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)}.\end{aligned}
$$

At the point where $t=\dfrac{\pi}{4},$ the slope $m$ of the tangent line is given by 

$$
\begin{aligned}m & ={\frac{dy}{dx}|}_{t=\pi /4} \\  & =-\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})+4\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})}{2(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4}))} \\  & =-\frac{\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{2}+4(0)}{2(0-\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{2})} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

To find the slope $m_n$ of the normal line, we take the negative reciprocal of $m$:

$$
m_n = -\dfrac{1}{m} = -\dfrac{1}{\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)} = -2
$$

Finally, to calculate the equation of the normal line, we use the point-slope form 

$$
y - y_1 = m_n(x-x_1),
$$

with

$$
(x_1,y_1) = \left(\sqrt{2}+1,\dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{2} -2\right), \qquad m_n=-2,
$$

and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y-(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}-2) & =-2(x-(\sqrt{2}+1)) \\ y-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}+2 & =-2x+2\sqrt{2}+2 \\ y+2x & =\frac{5\sqrt{2}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
